title: metric digits after a rounding carry
issue_text:
`humanize.metric` sometimes prints one digit more than `precision` asks for. With the default of 3 I expect three significant figures, but a value that rounds up past a power of ten gets four:

```python
>>> import humanize
>>> humanize.metric(9996)
'10.00 k'
>>> humanize.metric(99960)
'100.0 k'
>>> humanize.metric(9.9996)
'10.00'
```

Slightly larger inputs look right: `humanize.metric(10_400)` gives `'10.4 k'` and `humanize.metric(104_000)` gives `'104 k'`. I expected the three calls above to show three digits as well, i.e. `'10.0 k'`, `'100 k'` and `'10.0'`. Values that round all the way up into the next prefix already work, for example `humanize.metric(999.8, "W")` returns `'1.00 kW'`, and that should stay as it is.
